Characters

Round 1 · reference won
Critic verdicts (1)
  1. R1RefCharacters' poses/facing and head proportions: the dad at the desk is rendered from directly behind (no visible face/beard, just a brown hair block on a plaid back) and the music kid is a stiff standing figure whose oversized lavender hat-head is ~60% of her height and hides her face. Per the reference: rotate/turn the dad to 3/4 profile, seated with arms forward typing, so beard+face read; shrink kids' heads to ~1:1.5 head:body chibi with hat sitting ON the head (ears on top, face fully exposed below brim), and pose the music kid sitting cross-legged on the rug playing with toys, the painter seated on a stool facing the easel with brush arm raised, and the beagle lying down chewing a bone with clear floppy ears, white muzzle and tan patches instead of the hunched sitting blob.

HUD

Round 1 · reference won
Critic verdicts (1)
  1. R1RefHousehold portrait cards (top-left): ours render the sim heads as small, soft, badly framed 3D captures - dad's face is cropped under hair, bunny-girl and cat-hat girl faces are tiny/washed out, dog is an unreadable smudge. Ref uses crisp, sharp, front-facing head-and-shoulders portraits filling ~85% of the white rounded card, face centred with clear eyes/smile, warm key light on a light backdrop. Fix the portrait camera (closer, eye-level, centred on face, no DOF/blur, higher render res). Secondary: action-bubble progress bars are stubby (~1/3 bubble width) and thin - make them span the full bubble width under the label, ~8px tall with rounded track like ref; add the missing season line under day/time in the clock panel.

House & lighting

Round 1 · reference won
Critic verdicts (1)
  1. R1RefCamera/framing and depth: ours is shot too close and top-down with no visible lower floor, so the railing borders blur instead of revealing the downstairs room; pull the home_day camera back and lower its pitch (~35-40 deg) to frame the whole upstairs open-plan room plus, past the balcony railing in the lower-left, a populated lower floor (bookshelves, table lamps glowing, sofa) like the reference. Also fill the bare floor/walls: add cork board with pinned notes and framed landscape painting above the desk, dual monitors+printer+mug on desk, tall bookshelf with globe/trophy, guitar next to keyboard, toy box and soccer ball, hanging vines. And cut the global orange/yellow grade (reduce saturation/warm tint and exposure, restore contrast and neutral wood tones; window should not blow out).

Backyard BBQ

Round 1 · reference won
Critic verdicts (1)
  1. R1RefSKY + BACKDROP: ours has no visible sky at all - the top third is a blurred flat dark-purple house wall/haze with no horizon. Pull the camera/house back or lower the house so a purple-to-orange sunset gradient sky (orange/pink glow at horizon, violet above, a few clouds) is visible across the top 20-25% of frame, and add a row of dark silhouetted voxel neighbour houses with a few warm lit windows plus dark tree silhouettes along the horizon behind the fence. Also reduce the purple DOF/fog wash on the house so its lit sliding glass doors (showing warm furnished interior) and pergola with string lights on posts read crisply.

Autumn festival

Round 1 · reference won
Critic verdicts (1)
  1. R1RefBackground/midground is lost in a blown-out yellow-orange haze: bloom+glow and depth-of-field blur are far too strong, so the town hall/clock tower, bunting, stage and crowd are unreadable smears and the whole frame has no value contrast. Cut bloom/glow intensity and DOF far-blur drastically (keep only mild blur past the fountain), lower exposure so cobbles are mid-grey-brown not beige-white, and then actually populate the backdrop per ref: a red-brick town hall with a crisp white clock face framed by large saturated orange/red voxel tree canopies on both sides, a raised wooden stage at back-right with a guitarist, maple-leaf banner and triangle bunting, string lights with discrete warm bulbs, black lamp posts with glowing lanterns, and a stone fountain centre-midground.

Grocery market

Round 1 · reference won
Critic verdicts (1)
  1. R1RefCamera/composition: the market preset camera sits too low and close, so the family fills the middle third and hides the store; the fridge cases, shelves and back aisles shrink to a thin distant strip. Per the reference, pull the camera back and up (about 1.6-2x the distance, looking down roughly 25-30 deg) so the characters are about 1/3 of the frame height, make the produce wall on the left readable as distinct voxel tomatoes/carrots/bananas/apples in crates with $ tags, show a full row of lit fridge cases with bottles and tall shelves of distinct cereal-box packs in the midground, add 3-5 background shoppers, and cut the heavy DOF blur and orange haze for brighter, neutral-warm lighting.
